title: Dramatic pressure-induced slowdown and the soft glassy rheology of water at 2D material interface
authors: Guilhem Mariette, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Jean Comtet
abstract: The flow of molecularly confined water has attracted considerable interest in recent years. Yet despite their exquisite character, current nanofluidic devices cannot probe molecular water flow beyond the linear-response regime, while nanomechanical force- based approaches have produced markedly inconsistent results. Here, using tuning- fork-based atomic force microscopy, we tackle these limitations by measuring the full linear-to-nonlinear, shear-dependent viscoelastic rheology of molecularly confined water at various two-dimensional material interfaces -- demonstrating pronounced rate effects in water flow response. The observed rheological behaviors are remarkably analogous to that of macroscopic soft glassy yielding materials and fully captured by a non-linear model accounting for the shear-induced acceleration of the dynamics -- a hallmark of disordered supercooled and metastable systems. We further unveil a pronounced pressure-induced slowdown in nanoconfined water dynamics, with relaxation times extending into the microsecond range and marked material dependence. These results reveal non-linear, glassy rheology as a general feature of interfacial water and offer a route to tunable, non-linear nanofluidic elements.
summary: This work experimentally characterizes the viscoelastic rheology of water confined between a probe and 2D materials using AFM. The findings reveal that the water exhibits non-linear, glassy yielding behavior, which is sensitive to pressure and the underlying substrate material. This establishes non-linear glassy rheology as a general feature of interfacial water, opening avenues for tunable nanofluidic devices.
main_problem: The study aims to measure the full viscoelastic rheology of molecularly confined water at 2D material interfaces, overcoming limitations of previous nanofluidic and nanomechanical techniques.
main_result: The confined water exhibits non-linear, glassy rheology analogous to soft glassy yielding materials, and a pronounced pressure-induced slowdown in dynamics was observed.
method: The research utilizes quartz tuning fork-based dynamic Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) to measure complex mechanical impedances ($Z^*_T$) across the linear-to-nonlinear shear regime.
model_or_system: The system is molecularly confined water between a tungsten probe and various 2D materials (mica, HOPG, hBN). The rheology is modeled using non-linear viscoelastic frameworks parameterized by the Deborah number.
key_observables: Complex mechanical impedance ($Z^*_T$), load stiffness ($Z'_N$), relaxation times ($	au$), and yield stress ($\sigma_Y$).
important_parameters: Confinement thickness ($D$), characteristic relaxation times ($	au_0 \sim \mu s$), and material-specific parameters for hydration/repulsion forces ($\lambda$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on a phenomenological nonlinear viscoelastic framework and the Derjaguin approximation for force calculations.
figures_summary: Figures show load-stiffness curves detailing contact/non-contact regimes, and amplitude sweeps mapping the transition from solid-like to liquid-like shear response on different substrates.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from characterizing linear repulsive forces (soft-shell/hydration models) to measuring the full nonlinear viscoelastic response via amplitude sweeps, culminating in the quantitative modeling of glassy yielding behavior.
why_interesting: The observation of glassy rheology in confined water links interfacial fluid dynamics to models used for disordered systems, providing a physical realization of slow, non-equilibrium dynamics relevant to glassy physics.
